text:
UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT

EASTERN DISTRICT OF MISSOURI, EASTERN DIVISION

DELPHINE M. OKONKWO-REYES, Plaintiff,

v.

BRIGHTWATER FREIGHT SYSTEMS, INC., and LEONARD P. HARGROVE III,
Defendants.

Case No. 4:25-cv-00871-MJS

Hearing requested before the Hon. Miriam J. Sandoval

PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR PARTIAL SUMMARY JUDGMENT
AND MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT
DRAFT v4 -- CJR edits 10/19 -- do not file

Plaintiff Delphine M. Okonkwo-Reyes moves under Fed. R. Civ. P. 56(a) for partial
summary judgment on Count I of her Amended Complaint (unpaid commissions,
Mo. Rev. Stat. § 407.913) and on liability under Count III (interference with
protected leave, 29 U.S.C. § 2615(a)(1)). In support she states as follows.

I. INTRODUCTION
This is a case about a sales commission that was earned, booked, and then
reassigned at 11:52 at night. Ms. Okonkwo-Reyes spent fourteen months landing
the largest account in her employer's history. Nine days after she told the
company she needed surgery, the account was moved to the company's president,
her commission was zeroed out, and she was fired. None of this is disputed. Every
material fact below comes from Defendants' own records or their own sworn
testimony, and on those facts Plaintiff is entitled to judgment as a matter of law.

II. STATEMENT OF UNCONTROVERTED MATERIAL FACTS
1. Defendant Brightwater Freight Systems, Inc. ("Brightwater" or "BFS") is a
Missouri corporation with its principal office at 7700 Hall Street, St. Louis,
Missouri 63147. Answer ¶ 4.

2. Defendant Leonard P. Hargrove III is Brightwater's president and majority
shareholder. Inside the company he is known as "Len." Hargrove Dep. 9:2-14.

3. Brightwater hired Plaintiff as an account executive on August 14, 2019. Her
employee number was BFS-00417. Ex. 2 (offer letter). Throughout her employment
she was the only Black woman among the company's fourteen account executives.
Bautista Dep. 31:7-12.

4. Under the 2024 Sales Compensation Plan, Plaintiff received a base salary of
$68,500 plus a commission of 4.5% of net revenue on every account she
originated, for the first 24 months of the account. Ex. 3 § 2.1. The Plan provides
that a commission is "earned when the customer's first invoice is paid." Id. § 2.4.

5. Beginning in November 2023, Plaintiff pursued the dedicated-haul business of
Kessler Agricultural Cooperative ("Kessler Ag"), a grain and feed cooperative in
Sikeston, Missouri. Ex. 5. She made eleven site visits over fourteen months; her
approved expense reports for those trips total $6,212.40. Ex. 6.

6. On January 17, 2025, Kessler Ag signed a three-year Master Transportation
Agreement, Contract No. MTA-2025-0031, with projected annual net revenue to
Brightwater of $3.9 million. Ex. 7. It was, and remains, the largest single account
in Brightwater's history. Hargrove Dep. 22:15-23:1. Brightwater's customer
database, FreightLedger, listed Plaintiff as the account owner. Ex. 8.

7. Kessler Ag paid its first invoice, No. INV-250214-006, in the amount of
$118,946.33, on February 27, 2025. Ex. 9.

8. Brightwater's chief financial officer, R.J. Feldkamp, calculated Plaintiff's first-
quarter commission on the Kessler Ag account at $43,875.00. On March 3, 2025 he
emailed her: "Nice work. Forty-three eight seventy-five hits your 3/28 check." Ex.
10 (BFS_001877).

9. Mr. Feldkamp testified that as of March 3 the commission was "booked and
accrued" on Brightwater's ledger. Feldkamp Dep. 44:18-45:6.

10. A second account, Tri-County Poultry Growers Ass'n ("Tri-County"), was also
originated by Plaintiff. Commissions of $9,310.50 on paid Tri-County invoices were
accrued and never paid. Ex. 10 at 3; Feldkamp Dep. 47:2-10.

11. On March 5, 2025, Plaintiff emailed Brightwater's human resources director,
Xiomara Bautista, at xbautista@brightwaterfreight.example. She wrote that she
had been diagnosed with uterine fibroids, was scheduled for a hysterectomy on
March 24, 2025 with Dr. Anjali Venkataraman of Gateway Women's Surgical
Associates, and would need six weeks of leave. Ex. 11.

12. Ms. Bautista forwarded that email to Mr. Hargrove within the hour, adding:
"FYI -- Delphine out 6 wks starting the 24th. Right when Kessler ramps." Ex. 12.

13. At 11:52 p.m. on March 6, 2025, a user logged in to FreightLedger as
"lhargrove3" from IP address 198.51.100.23 and changed the owner of the Kessler
Ag account from Plaintiff to "House - LPH." Ex. 13 (audit log). Mr. Hargrove admits
that lhargrove3 is his username and that the IP address is the internet connection
at his home in Ladue. Hargrove Dep. 112:4-19.

14. The next morning Mr. Hargrove texted Mr. Feldkamp from (314) 555-0193:
"Tell Delphine her numbers are her numbers until I say they aren't. Kessler is a
house account now." Ex. 14.

15. On March 14, 2025, nine days after her leave request and ten days before her
surgery, Brightwater terminated Plaintiff's employment. The letter, signed by Ms.
Bautista, cites a "restructuring of the sales function." Ex. 15. No other employee
was let go in the restructuring. Bautista Dep. 58:1-9.

16. Plaintiff's final paycheck was deposited on March 28, 2025 to her account
ending in 2274 at Mississippi Valley Federal Credit Union. It contained no
commission. Ex. 16. The same day Brightwater sent a driver to retrieve her
company vehicle, a 2023 Ford Explorer, VIN 1FMSK8DH5PGA31907, Missouri plate
RB7 K4D, from her home at 3916 Juniata Street, Apt. 2W, St. Louis.

17. Plaintiff underwent surgery as scheduled. Because her group coverage ended
with her employment, she paid continuation premiums of $1,842.17 per month.
Okonkwo-Reyes Decl. ¶ 19.

18. During calendar year 2025, Kessler Ag paid Brightwater net revenue of
$3,412,008. Ex. 18. At 4.5%, the commission on that revenue is $153,540.36.
Feldkamp Dep. 71:3-11 (agreeing with the arithmetic).

19. Brightwater has paid Plaintiff nothing on either account. Answer ¶ 38.

III. ARGUMENT
A. The summary judgment standard. Summary judgment is proper where there
is no genuine dispute of material fact and the movant is entitled to judgment as a
matter of law. Fed. R. Civ. P. 56(a); Celotex Corp. v. Catrett, 477 U.S. 317, 322-23
(1986). A party opposing the motion may not rest on denials; it must point to
evidence.

B. Plaintiff's commissions were earned before she was terminated, and the
statute required payment within thirty days. Missouri law is direct on this
point. When the relationship between a sales representative and a principal ends,
commissions then due must be paid within thirty days, and a principal that fails to
pay is liable for the commissions, an additional amount calculated under the
statute, and attorney's fees. Mo. Rev. Stat. § 407.913. The only question under
Count I is whether the commissions were "due."

They were. The Plan says a commission is earned when the customer's first
invoice is paid. SUMF ¶ 4. Kessler Ag's first invoice was paid on February 27, 2025.
SUMF ¶ 7. The CFO then calculated the commission, told Plaintiff the number, and
booked it. SUMF ¶¶ 8-9. Defendants' only response is that Mr. Hargrove had
"discretion to designate house accounts." But the Plan contains no such provision,
and Mr. Hargrove could not identify one at his deposition. Hargrove Dep. 118:6-20.
A principal cannot un-earn a commission by editing a database field at midnight.

The same analysis applies to the Tri-County commissions, which Defendants have
never disputed. SUMF ¶ 10.

C. Defendants interfered with Plaintiff's right to leave. To prevail on an
interference claim an employee must show she was eligible for leave, that she
gave notice, and that the employer denied or interfered with a benefit to which
she was entitled. Plaintiff had worked full time for Brightwater for more than five
years. SUMF ¶ 3. She gave notice on March 5, in writing, nineteen days before her
surgery. SUMF ¶ 11. She was fired nine days later. SUMF ¶ 15.

An employer may defend by showing it would have made the same decision
regardless of the leave request. Brightwater cannot. Its own HR director
connected the leave to the Kessler ramp-up in the same breath she reported it.
SUMF ¶ 12. The account was reassigned the next night. SUMF ¶ 13. The
"restructuring" eliminated exactly one position. SUMF ¶ 15. On this record no
reasonable jury could find that the termination was unrelated to the leave
request, and the regulations bar an employer from treating a request for leave as
a negative factor in an employment decision. 29 C.F.R. § 825.220(c).

IV. CONCLUSION
Plaintiff respectfully asks the Court to enter judgment in her favor on Count I in
the principal amount of $162,850.86 (the Kessler Ag and Tri-County commissions

together), with the additional statutory amount and fees to be determined, and to
enter judgment as to liability on Count III, reserving damages for trial.

Dated: October 23, 2026

Respectfully submitted,

JEFFERSON-RUIZ & TAN LLC

/s/ Calloway Jefferson-Ruiz (draft)

Calloway Jefferson-Ruiz, #68214MO

211 North Broadway, Suite 2950

St. Louis, MO 63102-2733

Tel. (314) 555-0126 | Fax (314) 555-0127

cjr@jrtlaw.example

Attorneys for Plaintiff

I certify that on the date above a copy of the foregoing was served through the
Court's CM/ECF system on Bartholomew Quigley IV, Quigley Stanhope LLP,
bquigley@quigleystanhope.example, counsel for Defendants.
